info_cards.title: Famous Photograph: Migrant Mother

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: American Progress
info_cards.fact: "American Progress" by John Gast. A 19th-century allegorical painting symbolizing westward expansion in the United States.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Whistlejacket
info_cards.fact: "Whistlejacket" by George Stubbs. A life-size portrait of a rearing racehorse against a plain background.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Blue Boy
info_cards.fact: "The Blue Boy" by Thomas Gainsborough. An 18th-century English portrait of a boy dressed in blue satin clothing.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Basket of Apples
info_cards.fact: "Basket of Apples" by Paul Cezanne. A still-life painting exploring shape and perspective through everyday fruit and objects.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Tower of Babel
info_cards.fact: "The Tower of Babel" by Pieter Bruegel the Elder. Shows a massive, fantastical tower under construction based on the Bible story.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Wheatfield with Crows
info_cards.fact: "Wheatfield with Crows" by Vincent van Gogh. A dramatic landscape with a stormy sky over a golden wheat field.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp
info_cards.fact: "The Anatomy Lesson of Dr. Nicolaes Tulp" by Rembrandt. An early group portrait showing surgeons studying anatomy.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Madame X
info_cards.fact: "Madame X" by John Singer Sargent. A formal portrait of a Parisian socialite in an elegant black gown.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Whistler's Mother
info_cards.fact: "Whistler's Mother" by James McNeill Whistler. Formally titled Arrangement in Grey and Black, it shows the artist's mother seated in profile.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Fighting Temeraire
info_cards.fact: "The Fighting Temeraire" by J. M. W. Turner. Shows an old warship being towed to be scrapped, painted with glowing colours.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: The Charioteer of Delphi
info_cards.fact: "The Charioteer of Delphi" by Ancient Greek sculptor. A bronze statue of a chariot racer, remarkably well preserved from ancient Greece.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Boy with Thorn
info_cards.fact: "Boy with Thorn" by Ancient Roman sculptor. A small bronze statue of a boy pulling a thorn from his foot.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: The Capitoline Wolf
info_cards.fact: "The Capitoline Wolf" by Etruscan/Italian sculptors. A bronze statue of a wolf nursing the legendary twins Romulus and Remus, a symbol of Rome.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Pieta
info_cards.fact: "Pieta" by Michelangelo. A marble sculpture showing the Virgin Mary cradling the body of Jesus, in St. Peter's Basilica.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Moses
info_cards.fact: "Moses" by Michelangelo. A large marble statue of the biblical figure Moses, located in Rome.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Bacchus
info_cards.fact: "Bacchus" by Michelangelo. One of Michelangelo's early marble sculptures, depicting the Roman god of wine.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Perseus with the Head of Medusa
info_cards.fact: "Perseus with the Head of Medusa" by Benvenuto Cellini. A bronze Renaissance statue in Florence depicting a scene from Greek mythology.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Hercules and Cacus
info_cards.fact: "Hercules and Cacus" by Baccio Bandinelli. A large marble statue in Florence's Piazza della Signoria depicting a mythological hero.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Neptune Fountain (Bologna)
info_cards.fact: "Neptune Fountain (Bologna)" by Giambologna. A grand bronze fountain sculpture of the sea god Neptune in Bologna, Italy.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Mercury (Giambologna)
info_cards.fact: "Mercury (Giambologna)" by Giambologna. A graceful bronze statue showing the messenger god appearing to fly upward.

info_cards.title: Famous Person: Malala Yousafzai

info_cards.title: Book Summary: Silent Spring
info_cards.fact: "Silent Spring" by Rachel Carson (1962) documented how the pesticide DDT was harming birds and wildlife, and is widely credited with leading to the creation of the US Environmental Protection Agency.

info_cards.title: Book Summary: Guns, Germs, and Steel
info_cards.fact: "Guns, Germs, and Steel" by Jared Diamond examines how geography, agriculture, and disease shaped the rise of different societies throughout history.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Abraham Lincoln
info_cards.fact: "Government of the people, by the people, for the people." — 16th president of the United States who led the country through the Civil War and helped end slavery.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: George Washington
info_cards.fact: "It is better to offer no excuse than a bad one." — American general and the first president of the United States, who led the colonies to independence from Britain.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Thomas Jefferson
info_cards.fact: "I cannot live without books." — Third U.S. president and principal author of the Declaration of Independence.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Benjamin Disraeli
info_cards.fact: "The secret of success in life is for a man to be ready for his opportunity when it comes." — British statesman who served as Prime Minister and was a prominent novelist.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Winston Churchill
info_cards.fact: "Success is not final, failure is not fatal: it is the courage to continue that counts." — British prime minister who led the United Kingdom through the Second World War.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Queen Elizabeth I
info_cards.fact: "I know I have the body of a weak and feeble woman, but I have the heart and stomach of a king." — Queen of England whose long reign (1558-1603) is remembered as a golden age of English culture and exploration.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Queen Victoria
info_cards.fact: "We are not interested in the possibilities of defeat." — British monarch whose long reign saw vast industrial, cultural, and territorial growth of the British Empire.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Catherine the Great
info_cards.fact: "I praise loudly. I blame softly." — Empress of Russia who expanded the Russian Empire and championed arts and education.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Simon Bolivar
info_cards.fact: "A people that loves freedom will in the end be free." — South American military and political leader who helped lead several countries to independence from Spain.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Toussaint Louverture
info_cards.fact: "I want liberty and equality to reign throughout Saint-Domingue." — Leader of the Haitian Revolution who helped establish Haiti as the first Black-led republic.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Otto von Bismarck
info_cards.fact: "Politics is the art of the possible." — Prussian statesman who united the German states into the German Empire in 1871.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Theodore Roosevelt
info_cards.fact: "Do what you can, with what you have, where you are." — 26th U.S. president known for conservation efforts and progressive reforms.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Franklin D. Roosevelt
info_cards.fact: "The only thing we have to fear is fear itself." — 32nd U.S. president who led the country through the Great Depression and most of World War II.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Eleanor Roosevelt
info_cards.fact: "No one can make you feel inferior without your consent." — American diplomat and activist who championed human rights and helped draft the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Nelson Mandela
info_cards.fact: "It always seems impossible until it's done." — South African leader who spent 27 years in prison for opposing apartheid and later became the country's first Black president.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Desmond Tutu
info_cards.fact: "Do your little bit of good where you are; it's those little bits of good put together that overwhelm the world." — South African archbishop and human-rights activist who fought against apartheid.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Wangari Maathai
info_cards.fact: "When we plant trees, we plant the seeds of peace and seeds of hope." — Kenyan environmental and political activist who founded the Green Belt Movement and won the Nobel Peace Prize.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Aung San Suu Kyi
info_cards.fact: "Please use your freedom to promote ours." — Burmese politician and democracy advocate who spent years under house arrest for opposing military rule.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Jawaharlal Nehru
info_cards.fact: "The light has gone out of our lives... yet the light that shone in this country was no ordinary light." — India's first prime minister who led the country in its early years of independence.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Indira Gandhi
info_cards.fact: "You cannot shake hands with a clenched fist." — India's first female prime minister who served for over fifteen years across two terms.
